{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=1 \\  & {x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=-1 \\  & {x}_{3}=3\end{aligned}

activity_context.topic_title: Solving Systems of Equations Using Back Substitution

feedback.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:
    

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=2 \\  & {x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-\frac{1}{2} \\  & {x}_{3}=-1\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
The third equation states that ${x}_{3}=-1.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}+(-1)=-\frac{1}{2}\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-\frac{1}{2}+1=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}$ and ${x}_{3}=-1$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}-2(\frac{1}{2})+(-1)=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2+1+1=4.
$$

Therefore, the solution is ${x}_{1}=4$, ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}$, and ${x}_{3}=-1.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨4,\frac{1}{2},-1⟩.$
